document_title: Paddy / Rice (Jhona/Dhan) Disease and Insect Pest Advisory

sections.section_title: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB / Peela Jhulsa) in Paddy
sections.disease_pest_name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)
sections.symptoms: Water-soaked translucent lesions starting from leaf tips and margins, progressing downwards with wavy margins. Lesions turn yellow to straw-colored. In severe cases, wilting known as Kresek stage occurs.
sections.recommended_action: Avoid excessive nitrogen/urea application which aggravates BLB. Drain excess water from the affected field for 3-4 days. Spray Streptocycline @ 15 g plus Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 500 g in 200 liters of water per acre. Note: Antibiotic sprays have preventive efficacy only.
sections.preventive_measures: Sow resistant/tolerant varieties such as PR 126, PR 121, or Pusa Basmati 1847. Practice balanced NPK with recommended potash.

sections.symptoms: BPH nymphs and adults congregate at the base of rice tillers just above the water level. Severe infestation results in circular drying patches in fields called 'hopper burn'.
sections.recommended_action: Monitor tiller bases weekly. When ETL of 5-10 hoppers per hill is observed, spray Pymetrozine 50% WDG @ 120 g per acre or Triflumezopyrim 10% SC @ 94 ml per acre. Direct spray strictly towards the base of the plants using a hollow cone nozzle.
sections.preventive_measures: Drain water for 2-3 days during peak pest activity. Strictly avoid synthetic pyrethroids (like Cypermethrin or Deltamethrin) as they trigger extreme BPH resurgence by eliminating natural spiders.

sections.symptoms: Oval or elliptical greenish-grey spots on leaf sheaths near water level. Spots enlarge with irregular dark brown margins like snake skin pattern.
sections.recommended_action: Spray Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG (Nativo) @ 80-100 g or Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 400 ml in 200 liters of water per acre at early disease appearance.
sections.preventive_measures: Keep bunds clean of grassy weeds. Avoid dense planting and excessive nitrogen.
